configs.description: The barebone as Supermicro sells it: ten drive trays, both 860 W supplies, both risers with all three slots blanked.
configs.name: base

configs.description: A card in each slot, to show what the windows take: two-port full-height cards in slots 1 and 2 and a low-profile card in slot 3 (three of the library's ConnectX cards - not a Supermicro-qualified build). The photographed server carries a two-port card in slot 1.
configs.name: cards

configs.description: Bays 0 to 3 fitted with the orange-tab NVMe tray (MCP-220-00167-0B) in place of the standard tray; the rest as the base.
configs.name: nvme

gaps.note: no maximum system power on the product page, datasheet, manual or quick reference guide; the Lot 9 addendum gives only an idle figure, 260.43 W, for its tested configuration. The server profile's power requirement is unmet for that reason.
gaps.wanted: a configured maximum power figure from Supermicro for the SYS-111E-WR

gaps.note: the legends printed under the rear ports are not drawn: the only straight-on rear image held is 2 px/mm and resolves no printing at all, so what the plate says is unread. The power supplies' own labels are unread for the same reason.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on rear photograph of a SYS-111E-WR at 6 px/mm or better

gaps.note: the manual names the two risers only as the 1U LHS and RHS WIO riser cards and the product page lists neither; their RSC part numbers are not in any document held, so the riser parts are named for the chassis.
gaps.wanted: the riser card part numbers from the system's parts list

gaps.note: both faces are measured off photographs taken from slightly above the server at about 2 px/mm; positions across are good to a millimetre and positions down, and every part's height, somewhat worse. Vent slot and hole sizes are approximate.
gaps.wanted: square-on photographs of the front and rear, or a dimensioned drawing of the CSE-116BTS chassis

gaps.note: the optional black front bezel MCP-210-11601-0B (product page parts list) is not drawn; no image of it is held.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on image of the bezel on this chassis

gaps.note: the interior under the top cover is drawn from one top-down photograph at 1.5 px/mm that is 2.4% wider at the front than at the rear. Drawn: the cover (it lifts off), the board, eight DIMMs, the heatsink, the air shroud and the supply cage cover (both lift off), five fans in their tray, the power distribution box beside them (a plain box with its warning label), and standing in from the rear bays the two supplies, both risers and any cards in their slots. Not drawn: the ten drives and their cage (a plain fixed cover here, as photographed), the backplane (a line) and cabling. THE AIR SHROUD IS ESTIMATED: it is in one angled photograph only. The two risers are outlines by eye, and the slot 3 riser is in neither photograph. The empty sixth fan housing is not a bay.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned plan of the CSE-116BTS interior, and the vendor's fan numbering

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor

one of `power-max-w`, `power-max-ac-w`, `power-max-dc-w` in `attrs.power`; one of `operating-temp`, `operating-temp-f2b`, `operating-temp-b2f` in `attrs.environmental` (profile `server` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on 27 bays (front 10, rear 4, top 13) - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

chassis.note: Product page, datasheet and manual Appendix B agree: 1.7 x 17.2 x 23.5 in, 43 x 437 x 597 mm, 1U, chassis CSE-116BTS-R000WNP. 437 is the body between the ear folds, which is how both photographs measure, so it is the body and not the rack face. No document says what the depth runs between.

controls.note: Manual figure 1-2 and its tables; see supermicro/control-panel-sc116b@1. The front USB ports are USB 3.2 Gen1 (product page, front view).

drive-numbering.note: Product page and datasheet front view, and the quick reference guide: bays 0 to 9, the lower bay of each column even and the upper odd, left to right - 1 over 0, 3 over 2, up to 9 over 8. The group is numbered from 0 as Supermicro numbers it. Nothing is printed on the metal beside the bays that the photograph resolves, and the photograph does resolve the 1.3 mm digits under the control panel's network marks, so no bay numerals are drawn.

ears.note: THE EARS ARE NOT DRAWN. On the front photograph each ear with its handle runs about 38 px outside the fold, 18.5 mm, 474 mm ear to ear at the body's scale. The control panel and both front USB ports sit on the body, not the ears.

environmental.note: Product page and manual Appendix B: operating 10 to 35 C, non-operating -30 to 60 C, operating relative humidity 8 to 80% non-condensing, non-operating 8 to 90%.

faces.note: Bottom, left and right are sized from the stated dimensions and declared empty: no document held shows any of them straight on.

front.note: Ten hot-swap bays in five columns of two, columns starting at 1.3 on an 80.65 pitch, rows at 10.3 and 27.3, each seating a 76.0 x 14.0 tray. Above them a strip of vent slots, 1.4..5.8 down, seven to a column, with the pull-out tag in place of the first five over column 1. Right of the drives, from 401.5, the control panel (lamps 8.1 down, buttons 18.4 down) and under it two USB 3.2 ports one above the other, centred at (418.6, 28.5) and (418.6, 36.6). The vent slot widths are read at 2 px/mm and are approximate.

gate-1-front.note: The front photograph passes the panel gate only loosely. The body between the ear folds is 894 px for 437 mm, 2.046 px/mm across; top to bottom it is about 88 px for 43 mm, 2.05 px/mm, but the camera is slightly above the server and the top edge of the face is soft against the lid, so the height is good to two pixels, 2%. Positions across are read at 2.046 px/mm; positions down are read at the same scale from the top edge at 338 px and are the softer figures. The five drive columns are a check on the across scale: they start at 150.75, 314.5, 479.5, 644.5 and 810.75 px, steps of 163.75, 165, 165 and 166.25 - an even 165 px, 80.65 mm.

gate-1-rear.note: The rear photograph is the same kind of image: the body is 889 px across for 437 mm, 2.034 px/mm, and about 87 px down from 348 px. Two known sizes check it: each power supply measures 53.5 x 39.3 mm for the product page's 54.5 x 40.25, and the two full-height slot plates centre 19.9 mm apart for the standard's 20.32. Positions are good to about a millimetre across and a little worse down.

interior.note: THE TOP VIEW IS THE CHASSIS UNDER ITS TOP COVER, rear at the top; the cover (supermicro/system-cover-sc116b@1) is seated and comes off in the viewer, and everything beneath it says it is under it. The interior is read off the top-down photograph of the open SYS-111E-WR embedded in its manual MNL-2490 as figure 1-5 (856 x 1050), on which the chassis is 660 px across at the rear for 437 mm (1.510 px/mm) and 900 px front to rear for 597 (1.508); at the front the chassis is 675 px across, 2.4% more, so it passes the panel gate at the rear and loosens toward the front. Positions across are read from the image centre at a scale that runs from 1.510 at the rear to 1.545 at the front, and positions front to rear at 1.508. THE BOARD IS PLACED FROM THIS IMAGE AND LAID OUT FROM A BETTER ONE: it lies 115.0..318.0 across and 13.5..343.5 from the rear, and its own layout is supermicro/system-board-x13sew@2, measured off the SYS-111E-FDWTR photograph at twice the resolution; this image agrees with that layout to 1.5 mm across and 4 mm front to rear. FIVE FANS AND ONE EMPTY HOUSING stand in a black tray 370 from the rear: read with the image brightened, the six positions lie at 59.0, 100.1, 142.5, 182.9, 224.0 and 264.5 across, an even 41.1 pitch, and the second from the left is an empty frame - the manual says five fans "plus one additional fan housing space". A FIRST VERSION DREW THE FIVE NEAREST THE SUPPLIES on a 45 pitch, off the unbrightened image, which is dark there; the SYS-511E-WR photograph, which shows the same arrangement plainly, is what sent this one back to be read again. The drive cage cover runs from 469.5 to the front. THE SUPPLIES, THE RISERS AND THE CARDS ARE NOT PLACED IN THIS VIEW: each is seated in its rear bay and projects here through that bay's `plan:`, at the bay's own position mirrored from the rear (a blank projects nothing, so the base build shows the risers empty and the `cards` example shows three cards). The supplies' tops read 6 mm outward of that on this image, as parts standing nearer the camera do.

lifecycle.note: Searched 2026-10-04 for an end-of-life notice (Supermicro's product page, which still offers the system, and the web for "SYS-111E-WR end of life"); none found.

power.note: NO MAXIMUM SYSTEM POWER IS STATED on the product page, the datasheet, the manual or the quick reference guide; each gives the supply rating only. The Lot 9 addendum states the idle state power at the higher boundary temperature of the operating class, 260.43 W, for its tested configuration - an idle figure under one regulation's test, not a maximum - and it is not written as power-max. A supply rating is not the server's draw.

psus.note: Product page and manual Appendix B: two PWS-861A-1R, 860 W, redundant 1+1, Titanium; rear view table: PWS1 on the left, PWS2 on the right. Both are seated by default - the server ships with both.

rear.note: From the rear photograph, left to right: the two power supplies, PWS1 at 5.2 and PWS2 at 62.0; from 118.1 the I/O plate - a four-row vent field, the serial port (centre 148.2, 32.2), the BMC LAN port (173.6, 12.3) over two USB 2.0 ports (173.7; 23.5 and 32.2), two more vent rows over two blue USB 3.2 ports (192.2), LAN1 (210.1, 30.8) and LAN2 (228.8, 30.8), VGA (256.2, 32.4) and a small vent block; above LAN2 and VGA the slot 3 window; from 298 the slot 1 and 2 bracket with its thumbscrew post; and a column of vents at the right end. Names and order are the manual's figure 1-3 and rear view table.

rear-legends.note: NO REAR LEGEND IS DRAWN. Faint marks show under the ports on the photograph at 2 px/mm and none can be read, and nothing else printed on that face resolves at that scale either, so this is a limit of the image and not a reading that the plate is blank. See the gap.

rear-uid.note: The manual's rear figure labels a Unit ID LED right of the VGA port. The photograph shows a small oblong lens at (287.4, 34.9), right of the vent block beside VGA, and that is where the lamp is drawn; the figure's arrow is the only thing that says this lens is it.

slots.note: Product page: 2 PCIe 5.0 x16 FHFL slots and 1 PCIe 5.0 x8 (in x16) LP slot. Manual section 3.9: slots 1 and 2 on the "1U LHS WIO riser card", slot 3 on the "1U RHS WIO riser card". The slots are bays of the two riser parts (supermicro/riser-wio-lhs-x13sew@1, supermicro/riser-wio-rhs-x13sew@2), each a standard bracket behind a window, so the library's cards seat in them.

sources.note: Read for this model: Supermicro's product page for the SYS-111E-WR (supermicro.com/en/products/system/wio/1u/sys-111e-wr) and its two-page datasheet, for dimensions, weight, ports, slots, power supply and environmentals; the User's Manual MNL-2490 revision 1.0d, for the front, control panel and rear figures, LED tables, slot and riser descriptions and Appendix B; the quick reference guide QRG-2490; the Lot 9 addendum to the manual; the X13SEW motherboard manual MNL-2413; and two near straight-on photographs from StorageReview's review of the server - the front (storagereview.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/StorageReview-Supermicro-Sys-111E-WR-7.jpg, 1200 x 698) and the rear (storagereview.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/StorageReview-Supermicro-Sys-111E-WR-6.jpg, 1200 x 677). EVERY SUPERMICRO IMAGE OF THIS SERVER IS A PERSPECTIVE VIEW WITH CALLOUTS (product page, datasheet, manual figures 1-1 and 1-3, 960 x 720 at most); they are read for what is on each face and in what order, never for position. No vendor 3D model is on the product page, and NetBox's devicetype-library has no entry for this model or its chassis.

weight.note: Product page: net weight 21 lbs (9.53 kg), gross 33.5 lbs (15.2 kg). The page does not say what is installed at the net figure; the system is sold as a barebone, without processor, memory or drives.
